Glue code for fddev quic-trace, joining remote tile state and dumping QUIC config and connections.

# Purpose
This file implements the `fddev quic-trace` command. It is a diagnostic entry point that joins a target tile in read-only mode, reads QUIC state from shared memory, and prepares the data needed to trace either packet flow or error events. The code parses command-line options such as `--event`, `--dump`, `--dump-config`, `--dump-conns`, and `--send-tile`, then selects the target `quic` or `send` tile from the topology and sets up the local trace context.

The main function, [`quic_trace_cmd_fn`](<#quic_trace_cmd_fn>), connects to the target tile objects, rebuilds pointer references for non-relocatable shared-memory data, and joins the QUIC object and log buffer. It also scans all QUIC connections, prints configuration and connection state when requested, and builds a peer connection ID map for later lookup. Before starting the trace loop, it redirects metric writes to local buffers so the read-only trace does not modify the target topology. The file ends by dispatching to `fd_quic_trace_rx_tile` for stream tracing or `fd_quic_trace_log_tile` for error tracing, and it registers the `quic-trace` action as a diagnostic command.
